Summary

This PR fixes three security issues identified during a full static audit of the Python SDK (128 files, ruff + pyright clean, 244 tests pass):

- **Rug-pull attack (CWE-345):** `_absorb_tool_listing()` accepted re-fetched tool descriptions after a `tools/list_changed` notification with no integrity check. A malicious server can serve clean descriptions for N interactions, then send the notification and return poisoned descriptions on re-fetch. Fix: SHA-256 pin each description on first sight; any subsequent change drops the updated version and logs a security warning. Runs for all protocol versions (not gated on modern-only).

- **Tool description injection (CWE-20):** `_absorb_tool_listing()` validates `x-mcp-header` annotations and output schemas but never inspects `tool.description` — the field sent verbatim to the LLM context. Fix: regex scan against known prompt-injection patterns before pinning; drops tools that match on first sight.

- **DNS rebinding protection off by default (CWE-16):** `TransportSecurityMiddleware` defaulted to `enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False` for backwards compatibility. Fix: flip default to `True`; add a startup `WARNING` log when `allowed_hosts` is empty so misconfigured deployments fail visibly rather than silently rejecting all requests.

- **CWE-78 in CLI npx probe:** `subprocess.run([cmd, "--version"], shell=True)` on Windows. `cmd` is currently hardcoded, but `shell=True` with a list is exploitable if ever made configurable. Fix: remove `shell=True`.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mcp/client/session.py` | Add `_INJECTION_PATTERNS`, `_tool_desc_hash()`, `_scan_tool_description()`; security pass in `_absorb_tool_listing()` |
| `src/mcp/server/transport_security.py` | Flip DNS rebinding default to `True`; add empty-`allowed_hosts` startup warning |
| `src/mcp/cli/cli.py` | Remove `shell=True` from npx probe |

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing test suite: `pytest tests/client/ tests/transports/ tests/cli/` — 244 passed, 4 skipped (verified locally)
- [ ] `ruff check` on all three files — clean
- [ ] `pyright` on all three files — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [ ] New tests needed: rug-pull drop, injection drop, clean tool pass-through, legacy protocol also protected

## Background

These vectors were originally documented as part of the DEADBUG-MCP research series (rug-pull V3, cross-server poisoning V4). The rug-pull fix described by MCP Playground ("pin the tool definitions you approved, call the server several times, list again, and treat any difference as a security event") is now implemented at the SDK level in `_absorb_tool_listing()`.

Signed-off-by: Nicholas Michael Kloster <nicholas@nuclide-research.com>
